newsitem.title: UK: Glaxo off as R&D briefing fails to excite.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo off as R&D briefing fails to excite.

text.p: Shares in Glaxo Wellcome Plc traded lower on Friday after a research briefing failed to stimulate buying interest in a stock consolidating after a recent record high, dealers said.
Glaxo shares were down 19 pence, or 1.59 percent, to 1,176p by 0840 GMT in volume of 1.5 million while the FTSE-100 index was 12.6 points, or 0.28 percent, lower at 4432.4.
"The stock's had a very good run recently and while the R&D came up to expectations it's still been marked lower with the uncertainty after the election," a marketmaker at a British bank said.
Glaxo set a record closing high of 1,213.5p on Wednesday, after an intra-day peak at 1,215p.

Glaxo said in a research and development update that ten new drug molecules had entered development in the first four months of 1997 and it expected to have more than 20 in development by the end of the year.
Deputy chairman and chief executive Richard Sykes said the company was on track to meet its prediction of double-digit sales growth in 1999.
Glaxo's patent on leading ulcer drug Zantac runs out in June and generic rivals are set to enter the market.
Other drug companies 0#.FTPH were little changed, with the exception of SmithKline Beecham Plc which was off 9.5p (0.29 percent) at 989p.
Britain's Labour Party won a landslide victory in Thursday's election, ousting the Conservative Party from power after 18 years in office.
